newsitem.title: UK: BP, Shell up with oil price, U.S.Q3.
newsitem.headline: BP, Shell up with oil price, U.S.Q3.

text.p: Shares in British Petroleum and Shell Transport and Trading rose on Monday in tandem with crude oil prices and in anticipation of positive earnings surprises in the U.S. later today, dealers said.
BP was up 7p at 685-1/2p and Shell rose 7p to 10.44-1/2 stg.
December Brent crude reached a record high at the opening on Monday, up 18 cents at $24.71 a barrel to top its previous contract high by 11 cents.
"BP will see the greater benefit," said one analyst.
"Most of its operating profits come from exploration and production, where the price rise will improve margins."
Analysts said Shell was seeing the added benefit from switching in the sector.
Shares were also buoyed in anticipation of better-than-expected third quarter earnings from the U.S. oil majors later today, despite expectations already raised by the oil price strength.
Among those scheduled to report in the U.S. are Mobil, Texaco, Chevron and Exxon.
In the UK, third quarter earnings from Royal Dutch/Shell group are due October 31, and British Petroleum will post profits on November 5.
